findings.evidence: Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing. The employee receives a confirmation email once processing finishes. [...] Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request.
findings.fix: Restate the apply process as one ordered sequence, with the summary review and submission step placed unambiguously before or after the manager/finance sign-off, not both.
findings.violation: The section states two contradictory orderings of the same submission step: paragraph 2 says the request already moves through manager sign-off, finance confirmation, and final processing before the employee's confirmation email arrives, while paragraph 3 says the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request, as if submission has not yet happened. A reader cannot resolve which order actually governs, so they cannot tell whether to submit before or after approval.

findings.evidence: Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears.
findings.fix: Split the paragraph by reader: keep the employee's "you" actions together, and state the manager's countersignature step with an explicit subject ("The manager countersigns...") in its own sentence or section.
findings.violation: The paragraph addresses the employee directly as "you" in the first and third sentences, then switches without warning to an imperative ("Countersign the employee request") whose actor is a different reader, the approving manager, with no signal marking the shift, so a reader cannot tell which sentences describe their own actions and which describe someone else's.

findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review.
findings.fix: Pick one term for the thing being purchased and reimbursed, and use it in every sentence of this paragraph.
findings.violation: Three different terms, the stipend item, the reimbursable item, and the covered purchase amount, are used across three consecutive sentences for what appears to be the same single thing, with no stated equivalence, so a reader cannot tell whether the paragraph describes one item moving through three steps or three different items.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.
findings.fix: Rewrite the opening sentence to state the topic the rest of the paragraph covers.
findings.violation: The paragraph's opening sentence shares almost no vocabulary with the rest of the paragraph, so it does not preview the paragraph's actual topic.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Remove the three unrelated sentences, or move each to a section its topic actually belongs to, so the section covers only stipend-request coordination.
findings.violation: After its opening sentence, the section moves through three unrelated topics, a past travel-expense audit, evolving federal remote-work guidance, and the office coffee budget, with nothing connecting any of them to stipend-program coordination or to each other, so a reader finishing the section could not state what it is actually about.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Keep one subject running through the paragraph, or add explicit signals connecting each new subject back to the paragraph's stated topic.
findings.violation: Each of the section's four sentences changes its grammatical subject, benefits team, then audit, then federal guidance, then coffee budget, and none of the later three picks up the topic the sentence before it established, so the reader has to re-orient at every sentence boundary.

findings.evidence: Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt.
findings.fix: Move this section, or fold its content, into How to Apply, next to the other steps that begin the request.
findings.violation: This sentence describes the starting point of the request process, but the Request Steps section sits after How to Apply, Approval Timeline, Required Documentation, Reimbursement Amounts, Restrictions and Exceptions, and Terminology Notes, so a reader reaches the description of how the process begins only after reading six sections of later-stage and unrelated material.

findings.evidence: Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing.
findings.fix: Move the interrupting clause elsewhere, or split it into its own sentence.
findings.violation: 3 comma-set-off clause(s) totalling 14 words intervene between the sentence's apparent subject and its verb.

findings.evidence: An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The...
findings.fix: Open the paragraph with a transition word that states its relationship to the prior paragraph.
findings.violation: The paragraph opens with none of the fixed transition words, so the reader is not told how it relates to the paragraph before it.

findings.evidence: Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt.
findings.fix: Name the employee as the subject: "The employee begins the request by confirming eligibility and uploading a receipt."
findings.violation: The sentence's subject, "Completing the request," is a nominalized abstraction standing in for the employee who actually completes it, even though the sentence is grammatically active.

findings.evidence: Also, the benefits team reviews the reimbursement log on the first business day of the month. The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it.
findings.fix: Name explicitly which record the versioning rule applies to, for example "The most recent version of the reimbursement log supersedes the one before it."
findings.violation: "The most recent version" opens the second sentence with information the paragraph never established: the prior sentences name an equipment catalog and a reimbursement log but never call either one a "version," so the reader cannot tell which of the two the sentence means.
